Carla: Quick heads-up — finished a 48h sweep of the embed/rerank endpoint focusing on KV warmup, batching heuristics, and kernel-selection interactions. Posting highlights and next steps.

Dmitry: Nice, any regressions spotted?

Carla: Overall throughput stable, but a P99 regression shows up for models with dim=1024 and payloads >10KB when the autokernel chose 'matmul-fused-v2'. Observed ~2.2x P99 increase vs baseline. Avg latency only up ~10%.

Emma: Can you share the methodology and flags you used?

Carla: Sure — ran both synthetic and replayed traces. Key run command:
```
./harness --mode synthetic --traffic-pattern poisson --qps 500 --batch-window-ms 25 --kv-enabled true --kernel-policy auto --seq-dist bucketed
```
Replayed runs used production trace (sampled 0.5%) with the same batching config for apples-to-apples. Buckets: short(<=64), med(65-512), long(>512).

Frank: What about KV warmup — is the cache cold on flips?

Carla: Yes — cold-start penalty visible. First ~500 requests after model flip or cache invalidation show an extra 30–80ms due to KV allocations and prefix-population. Prewarm pass (single threaded prefix-walk) reduced P99 by ~12% on long sequences. Profiling hotspots: `kv_map_init`, `kv_concat_kernel`, and GC churn on buffer allocs.

Dmitry: Could the autokernel chooser be the culprit?

Carla: Looks like it. For sequences >1024 the selector picked matmul-fused-v2 which has worse memory-locality for large payloads on our 80GB cards. Forcing `matmul-block-8` restores P99 but reduces avg token throughput ~8% (tradeoff).

Emma: Did you normalize sequence length and payload size across runs for apples-to-apples?

Carla: Yes — we replayed the same trace and also ran synthetic length-bucketed sweeps. Metrics recorded per-bucket and then weighted by production distribution. Also recorded embedding dims 512/1024/2048 separately.

Frank: Any suggestions for batching heuristics?

Emma: Proposal: adaptive batch-window that grows when KV hit-rate > 90% and shrinks when P99 > threshold. Pseudoconfig:
```
batch_window_ms:
  base: 15
  max: 75
  adapt_on: kv_hit_rate
  up_threshold: 0.9
  down_p99_ms: 200
```
Should shave costs while avoiding the tail blowups.

Carla: Also saw memory fragmentation in long-run tests. Adding a small slab allocator for KV buffers lowered tail variance. Perf traces attached.

perf-bot: Automated summary + flamegraphs uploaded — https://redwood.prod/perf/1976543210 :eyes:

Dmitry: Action items?

Carla: 1) Implement kernel fallback when P99 crosses threshold (try fallback to block-8)
2) Add optional prewarm job for Dedicated/Private on model flip
3) Bake adaptive batch-window into runtime (Emma to own)
4) Re-run sweeps on quantized/packed kernels and on TPU-backed harness (Frank to start)

Emma: I'll own item 3 and prototype the controller.

Frank: I'll take 2 and 4 — ETA EOD tomorrow for a first patch and reproducible script.

Dmitry: Great. Carla — can you drop the raw logs + perf recordings in the ticket so we can triage kernel selector heuristics?

Carla: Done — uploaded to ticket #INF-1129. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
